correctness.rationale: The verifier exhausts every anonymous three-candidate profile through ten voters, every present ranking type, and every possible positive homogeneous abstention size. Two independent Coombs implementations agree on all tested states, and an independently organized event-first traversal reproduces exactly the same twelve minimal events. The two normalized ten-voter classes are directly checked. The exactly-two-identical-abstainer variant is independently exhausted through thirteen voters and yields exactly eighteen events in three relabeling classes.

evidence: Felsenthal's 2010 full text gives a fifteen-voter Coombs no-show example with two identical abstainers.
Felsenthal-Tideman defines participation in the ordinary one-voter form and includes Coombs among susceptible procedures.
Brandt-Matthäus-Saile's Coombs section explicitly states that, under the paper's tie-independent treatment, no-show may appear only if at least two voters abstain.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These sources dominate the qualitative existence question, so existence of Coombs no-show is not new. They do not imply the ten-voter one-abstainer boundary; indeed, the later two-abstainer assertion is contradicted by the verified ten-voter classes. Nor do they give the complete thirteen-voter boundary when exactly two identical abstainers are imposed.

evidence: The 2010 example demonstrates existence with fifteen voters and two abstainers but says nothing that would force a ten-voter lower boundary.
The standard participation definition permits a single voter to join or abstain, so excluding one-voter events is not entailed by the axiom itself.
The 2022 assertion that at least two abstainers are necessary is falsified by the two explicit ten-voter tie-independent classes.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The accepted claim is not a corollary or special case of prior work. Its one-abstainer boundary directly contradicts a prior restriction, and its exact profile and orbit counts require a complete finite classification. The exactly-two-abstainer refinement separately improves the known example under that added restriction.

originality.rationale: The closest literature gives a fifteen-voter Coombs no-show example, the standard single-voter participation formulation, and a later explicit assertion that tie-independent Coombs no-show needs at least two abstainers. The accepted ten-voter one-abstainer boundary therefore corrects a published claim, while the thirteen-voter two-abstainer boundary improves the older example under that stronger restriction. No inspected source states either complete finite census.
residual_risks: An unindexed correction, thesis, note, or software enumeration may already contain the same ten-voter or thirteen-voter census.
The LSE record reports online availability only at month resolution for April 2010; the metadata therefore uses the first exact documented public day, 27 May 2010, rather than inventing an April day.
The theorem excludes tied eliminations and tied final comparisons, so tie-breaking variants can have additional smaller-looking cases under different conventions.

value.rationale: Participation is a standard social-choice axiom and Coombs is a canonical elimination rule. The result corrects a specific published statement about the size of a no-show coalition, supplies the sharp tie-independent standard boundary, and also resolves the stronger exactly-two-abstainer variant. The exact profile and orbit classifications are therefore motivated structural facts at the first nontrivial boundary.
